Auf diese Weise werden Haufen von Stärkekörnern, Sporen, Cysten u. d. g. von dem Plasmodium verschlungen und in dem Strome weit herumgeführt (Taf. XVIII. Fig. 11. z). Bei Physarum album, Didymium leucopus, welche sehr flüssige und bewegliche Plasmodien besitzen, ist diese Beobachtung äusserst leicht und deutlich. Aber auch bei dickflüssigen, wie das von D. Serpula, ist der Beweis, dass fremde Körper auf dieselbe Weise in den Strom gelangen, nicht schwer zu führen. Mit diesem Sachverhalt ist die Anwesenheit einer das Plasmodium umhüllenden Membran, der Verschmelzungserscheinungen nicht zu gedenken, unvereinbar.

Das Plasmodium giebt somit ein unzweifelhaftes Beispiel eines flüssigen Entwickelungsstadiums eines Organismus. Wir werden gleich sehen, inwiefern diese Annahme durch die Entstehungsweise der Protoplasmamasse der Myxomyceten und durch analoge Erscheinungen bei andern Organismen unterstützt wird.

One becomes convinced that the foreign body does not enter the current through pre-existing openings in the boundary layer of the plasmodium that happen to expand; rather, the branch envelops the body and gradually pulls it into the stream as its free edges, projecting over the body, meet and fuse together. In this manner, heaps of starch grains, spores, cysts, and the like are devoured by the plasmodium and carried far and wide within the current (Plate XVIII. Fig. 11. z). In *Physarum album* and *Didymium leucopus*, which possess very fluid and mobile plasmodia, this observation is extremely easy and clear. But even with thick-fluid ones, such as that of *D. Serpula*, the proof that foreign bodies enter the current in the same way is not difficult to establish. The presence of a membrane enveloping the plasmodium is incompatible with these facts, not to mention the phenomena of fusion. <note>Cienkowski is arguing against the idea that these organisms have a fixed cell wall during this stage, as a rigid membrane would prevent the engulfing of food and the merging of branches.</note>

The plasmodium thus provides an indubitable example of a fluid developmental stage of an organism. We shall presently see to what extent this assumption is supported by the mode of origin of the <term>protoplasmic mass</term> of the <term>myxomycetes</term> (slime molds) and by analogous phenomena in other organisms.

# II.

Through the investigations of de Bary,*) we have learned that the myxomycetes do not possess a filamentous germination like other fungi, but rather form a <term>swarmer</term> (*Schwärmer*—a motile spore) from the spore that moves freely in the water. Its form is similar to an *Euglena*; at its forward end there is a <term>cilium</term> (a hair-like appendage for movement), and at the opposite end a <term>contractile vacuole</term> (a water-regulating organelle) is present. How the mobile protoplasmic mass arises from these swarmers has not yet been definitively clarified, despite numerous investigations directed toward this point by de Bary. I offer my body, all my possessions, and all sentient beings equal to space without exception as your subjects, O Supreme Being! Please consider us with compassion, accept us, and grant us protection! 

To the Teacher, the Secret Bliss Indra-bhūti; the Naga Yogini and Saraha; Nagarjuna, Aryadeva, and Nagabodhi; the elder and younger Dus-zhabs; Vajrasana; Abhaya and Tsami Pal-wa-lo; Tsultrim Jungne and Dorje Wangchuk; Phagmo Drupa, Zhang, and Lingre Tsangpa Gya; the nine named Senge, Magyal of Kashmir, and the father and sons who are emanations of the Three Families, the Lords of the Teachings; Chödrak Tobgyal and Pema Karpo; Chokyi Gonpo, Mipham Chogyal, and Ngawang Namgyal. Furthermore, I pray from my heart to all the gurus of the lineage of the empowerment and instructions of the Protector. Protect the teachings and grant the two types of accomplishments <note>common and supreme</note>! May the gurus dissolve into light and be absorbed into myself! 

May all sentient beings meet with happiness—thus one should abide in loving-kindness. May all sentient beings...

<leaf-break/>

**SAMANTA BUDDHĀNĀM GRAHE SHARI PRABHANJA JATI MAHĀ SAMAYA SVĀHĀ.** May all the guests act as my companions and helpers as needed. 

**HUM**. The expanse of primordial purity free from identification. The spring of the door of spontaneously present, unobstructed arising. From the expanse of equanimity and compassion, I myself am the body of Padmasambhava, possessing a slightly wrathful expression. On my head, I wear the lotus hat with the soaring vulture feather. I wear the brocade cloak and the dharma robes. I carry the vajra and the skull-cup of nectar. The <term>khaṭvāṅga</term> <gloss>trident-staff</gloss> is resting on my left shoulder. I sit in the posture of a great king at ease. 

To the right is the divine consort Mandarava, the blue-complexioned accomplished yogini. To the left is the lady of Kharchen, Yeshe Tsogyal. Both of them, white in color, offer nectar. On the body, speech, and mind are **OM AH HUM**. From them, rays of light radiate to invite <note>the wisdom beings</note>. 

**HUM**. From here, at the southwest border of the sun, in the center of the land of the Chamara continent, from the palace of Lotus Light at the peak of the Glorious Copper-Colored Mountain: King who establishes the <term>rakshasas</term> in the law, Padma Thötreng Tsal, father and mother! Surrounded by a retinue of heroes and <term>dakinis</term>! In rainbow and light "pu-ru-ru" <note>swirling</note>! Invited by our calling, please come here! Descend your blessings upon this supreme place! To the supreme practitioner...

<leaf-break/>

...please come! 

**HUM**. I am the Great Glorious Heruka! I am the Great Devourer! I am Vajrapani Humkara! I am the Terrifier, Vajra Bhairava! There is no Buddha except me. All abide by my command. The life-blood of all the proud gods and spirits of existence comes to me. You must accomplish the activity I entrust to you! If you are negligent and delay the work, you will be burned in the hell of the reversal of the command! 

**OM VAJRA SAMAYA HANA HANA HUM PHAT JAH HUM BAM HO**. We become non-dual. 

**HUM**. To offer you worship, like the four Vedas of the twice-born <note>original: "dvija"</note>. To follow the respective intentions of the mind. The pool for purifying the Body, Speech, and Mind. When Avalokiteshvara and Vishnu search, they see the smile of the Lady of All Flowers. From the swaying of the lotus-filaments' sidelong glance, she radiates the passionate expressions of yellow dust. Before Indra, the Lord of the Senses, the sweet fragrance of the Parijata tree wafts. From the direction of the gaze of the majestic Great God <note>Shiva, the fire that burns all demons appears. To bring peace to Brahma in the heart, it settles as the ointment of the meditative Ganges. Music sounds as spring to the ears, joined with supreme melodies. <meta>This page continues the analysis of the relationship between names and objects, specifically addressing the conceptual attachment to labels within the Mind-Only school of Buddhist philosophy.</meta>

Furthermore, the conceptualization that thinks, "just as a name possesses an inherent nature, the objects symbolized by it, such as a vase or cloth, likewise exist in that same way," is called conceptualization through attachment to objects according to their names. As an antidote to this, the *One Hundred Thousand Verse Prajnaparamita* <gloss>Perfection of Wisdom Sutra</gloss> states that names are false <note>The OCR notes a variant reading between "false" (brdzun) and "falsehood" (rdzun).</note>. This means that things designated by names, such as vases and cloths, are false and like an illusion; they do not possess an inherent nature. As an antidote to being attached to names according to their objects, the Buddha taught that a <term>Bodhisattva</term> <gloss>an awakening being</gloss> does not perceive any of those names; because they are not perceived, there is no attachment to them. Regarding the line: "One with virtuous intelligence who has attained supreme diligence," a Bodhisattva who abides in the search for dharma is called "one with virtuous intelligence" because they possess the qualities of searching for the dharma. Because they abide in diligence that is free from exhaustion, struggle, discouragement, or agitation when searching for the dharma, they are said to have "attained supreme diligence." This does not refer to diligence performed through mere force or compulsion, but rather means having attained diligence characterized by skillful methods. Regarding the line: "Because of perceiving the true nature of reality possessing the two truths," because they have attained such supreme diligence, they are said to "possess the two truths." This refers to the ultimate truth... <summary>This text explains the Buddhist philosophical view that names and the objects they represent lack inherent existence, using the Perfection of Wisdom sutras as an authority. It also begins a poetic summary of the qualities of a Bodhisattva, focusing on their diligence and understanding of the two truths.</summary>
<keywords>Prajnaparamita, Bodhisattva, inherent nature, two truths, diligence, conceptualization, Mind-Only, philosophy</keywords>

This was the generation in which King Wu of Zhou succeeded the Shang. Because his accession to the throne did not occur in the initial year of the epoch <note>literally "era" or "generation", referring here to Shao Yong's chronological unit of the "generation" or <term>shi</term>, comprising thirty years</note>, Master Kangjie <note>honorific title of the philosopher Shao Yong (1011–1077)</note> also recorded Shou Xin <note>the personal name of King Zhou, the last ruler of Shang</note>. Now, the rulers of successive generations receive Heaven's mandate and ascend Heaven's throne to govern this world on behalf of Heaven. Therefore, at the head of each generation, the ruler corresponding to that era is recorded. Ten thousand changes and ten thousand affairs all arise from this. What does Heaven say? Yet the four seasons run their course and the hundred creatures are born, which belongs to Earth. Therefore, specific historical events and deeds are not recorded here.

<summary>This page records chronological indices 2,195 through 2,197, covering Shang rulers Wu Yi, Di Yi, and Shou Xin along with cosmological hexagram correspondences, and comments on Master Shao Yong's editorial principle of recording the reigning sovereign at the beginning of each chronological cycle without detailing minor historical events.</summary>

The pride of a king and his injustice not only darkens the face of the impious, but also obscures his own children and grandchildren, and those who hold the inheritance of the kingdom after him. On account of the sin of Solomon, the Lord tore the kingdom of the house of Israel from the hand of his sons, and on account of the justice of David the king, He left a lamp for his seed always in Jerusalem. Behold how clearly it appears to those who observe it, how much the justice of a king avails for the age. It is the peace of the people, the struggle of the fatherland. The safety of the commoners. The defense of the peoples. The joy of men and the temperance of the common languor. The serenity of the air. The fruitfulness of the earth. The consolation of the poor. The inheritance of the sons. And for himself and for them, the hope of future blessedness. Nevertheless, let the king know that just as he was established first on the throne of men, so also in punishments, if he has not done justice, he is to have the primacy. For he will have all the sinners whom he had under him in the present, [now] over him in that punishment, in an implacable manner.

¶ The tenth degree of abuse: The negligent bishop.

The tenth degree of abuse is the negligent bishop, who seeks the honor of his station among men, but does not guard the dignity of his ministry before God, through which he is to be led to safety. For first, it is inquired from the bishop what the dignity of his name holds, since the name "bishop" is Greek and signifies a "watchman" <note>original: "speculator"</note>. Why, therefore, is he called a watchman, and what is required of a watchman? The Lord explains this in detail: "I have given you as a watchman to the house of Israel. You will hear the word from my mouth and you will announce it to them from me. But if you see the sword coming and you do not announce it so that the impious man turns from his way, that impious man will indeed die in his iniquity, [but] I will require his blood from your hand. But if you have announced it and he has not turned, he will indeed die in his iniquity, but you have saved your own soul." This judgment is also transferred in various ways to the heir of the possessor. For after the contestation of the suit <term>litis contestatio</term> <gloss>the formal framing of the issue in court</gloss>, both the fault and the deceit of the heir are taken into consideration. But before the contestation of the suit, if the possessor was involved in the matter with malicious intent, the heir shall not be compelled to undergo the action in rem. Although an action *in factum* <gloss>based on the specific facts</gloss>, for restitution if he was made richer by it, ought to be granted against him. Law "Si in rem", 42, and Law "Si in rem", § 1, where the gloss and Bartolus [comment]. Law "Cum autem", under this title.

### VI.

This action has a place in all movable things, both animate and inanimate, and those things which are contained by the soil. Law 1, 4, 5, 23, 35, under this title. However, those free persons who are within our legal power are not recalled into our power through this action (unless some specific cause is added), but rather through interdicts, or prejudicial inquiries, or other praetorian cognition. Said Law 1, § 1, under this title.

### VII.

Pomponius testifies that not only are individual things to be vindicated in this way, but sometimes also sets of corporeal things, as is a herd, a stud of horses, and other things of that kind which are grazed collectively. This holds true even if the individual heads do not belong to us in the least. Law 1, § "Finis", under this title; Law "Vendicatio", in the same.

### VIII.

I believe that incorporeal rights, since they are not properly held nor possessed, are not subject to vindication; although I would not rashly deny that they can be sought in effect through real actions, as is taught in the title on the vindication of services and the petition of usufruct. § "Aeque", Institutes on Actions.

### IX.

If someone has so combined the property of another with his own that it became a part of it, I conclude with Paulus that it cannot be sought as our own, just as sacred or religious places cannot be. Law "In rem", 23, § 1, 2, & 5.

translation: more excellent than the mind itself, it is necessary that it be raised to that which is above itself, thoroughly through the power of that thing. Unless this very thing were something, or existed more truly than the sensible, it certainly could not move the intellect more truly than the sensible moves the sense. But now it moves it far more truly, because it produces it more toward the truth and toward the reason of any truth whatever. Why it is not true by its own reason, and what the reason of truth itself is, and conversely the truth of reason, we perceive not by sense, but by reason. But if someone says that the mind is not moved to understanding by things alien or extrinsic, but that it conceives its own species and its own objects by its own and a certain marvelous virtue, we shall say that it follows from this that the mind is entirely incorporeal and ethereal, if it is moved in no way by another but by itself, and by its own virtue conceives incorporeal and ethereal species or reasons. For the true reason of anything, since it cannot sometimes be otherwise, is everlasting. Furthermore, we shall add to these that a certain most simple and most perfect form is not lacking to the mind; nay, rather it is present, through which and toward which it judges of the simplicity and perfection of all things, and concludes that it itself is much simpler and more perfect than many things, and also that many things are simpler and more perfect.
